meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so we'll be efficient. Who decided on that zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went into the gradebook?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero is based on.
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.

Show me that note with the date on it. "Like, being stuck" is a seventeen-year-old putting it in his own words, Hale, not a confession. Did he know at the time that this conversation could cost him his mark?
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.

I'm writing down October 15. Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft, Hale; that's what the outline is for. I want to see that outline next to the essay, so put both on the desk.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

You still haven't put the outline or your note in front of me, Hale. Whatever happens, this stays off his record and it stays quiet, nowhere near his classmates. Who else has seen this, and is anything on his file as of today?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you acknowledged entering the zero before contacting me, and you offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require copies of the October 15 outline and your November 2 note, confirmation of who else has seen this and that nothing is on Owen's file, and an assurance that the rewrite stays private and away from his class. I expect your written confirmation by Friday at 3 PM, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: fallback position, with nothing agreed yet; she still wants to see the outline and your note, to be told whether anything is on Owen's file and who else knows, and a promise that the rewrite stays private.
What moved her: owning the zero-before-the-call in one sentence and then giving dated details from Owen's own work, because they were specific and tied to his writing rather than to software.
What cost ground: describing the November 2 note and the October 15 outline without putting either in front of her, because she can't move on anything she can't check herself.
Try next time: when you bring up the October 15 outline, lay it on the desk beside the essay and answer her question about his file before you make the rewrite offer.
